attacks.claim: The automatic download replaces the local slot whenever the cloud copy is 'newer', which contradicts the artifact's own 'nothing is overwritten without that choice'. The artifact also never defines 'older' (device clock, server time, or version counter), and the clock-skew and missing-sync.meta cases are unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: 'On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older.' vs 'Nothing is overwritten without that choice.' ABSENT: definition of 'older' and clock-skew handling.

attacks.claim: The public patch note promises that saves on this PC stay put, but the auto-download path can replace the local slot without a prompt. Player-facing save-safety copy must match behaviour before it goes live on Steam and Epic.
attacks.evidence: 'Your saves on this PC stay where they are.' vs 'the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older'

attacks.claim: 'Every replaced version is kept' overstates retention. The server keeps only 5 versions per slot and the client keeps 3 local backups, so a version that rolls off both is gone. The artifact does not say which copy is authoritative when they diverge.
attacks.evidence: 'Every replaced version is kept: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally in saves/backup/.'

attacks.claim: The server accepts blobs without parsing or validating them, and only the client checks checksum and schema. A corrupt but under-2 MB upload can become the newest server version and push out the last good copies within 5 uploads. The client-side guard only prevents loading, not acceptance.
attacks.evidence: 'the server never parses them, accepts max 2 MB per slot' and 'the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot' ABSENT: server-side rejection of corrupt or empty newest versions.

attacks.claim: Each slot blob and the sync.meta sidecar are uploaded as separate operations with no stated atomicity or commit ordering. A partial failure can leave a blob and its metadata out of step, and the conflict logic then acts on inconsistent state.
attacks.evidence: 'Sync uploads the existing save slots plus a small sync.meta sidecar' ABSENT: atomicity or commit semantics.

attacks.claim: The steam_id to epic_account_id link is a persistent cross-platform identifier pair, but the artifact states no retention or deletion rule for the link row. The 24-month rule covers cloud data only, so the link may outlive the saves it served.
attacks.evidence: 'We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, sync.meta.' and 'Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted' ABSENT: link-row retention and deletion trigger.

attacks.claim: The 'no name' statement conflicts with the free-text device name in sync.meta, which often contains a real name. The 'We store' inventory also omits it, so the stated data inventory is inaccurate, and it feeds the privacy policy and store listing.
attacks.evidence: 'No email, name, payment or friends data.' alongside 'sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)'

attacks.claim: Age gating is described only for Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts. Steam accounts have no described minor check or consent mechanism, yet linking and sync send a persistent identifier and device name to an EU backend. The counsel review has no stated date or scope.
attacks.evidence: 'Epic under-13 (cabined) accounts get a restricted status from EOS; for them linking is not offered' ABSENT: Steam age gate or consent step; 'reviewed by our counsel (PP-v6)'

attacks.claim: The QA and beta evidence does not cover the shipped builds or production EOS. The Steam build was on a private branch, the Epic build ran on a dev sandbox, and the '0 lost saves' result comes from 2,300 opt-in Steam players and 150 Epic sandbox testers, against a 29% Epic base.
attacks.evidence: 'Steam build 18204411 on a private branch, Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox' and 'Epic sandbox testers (150). 0 lost saves'

attacks.claim: The 1.3 rollback was tested only on the Steam beta branch with one save. The Epic default-branch revert is untested. A 1.3 session that saves back is untested and may drop 1.4 modifier keys, silently changing difficulty, and that change then syncs. The artifact calls the rollback lossless, which the test does not show.
attacks.evidence: 'Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)' vs '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores' and 'saves written by 1.4 ... load in 1.3 (tested above)'

attacks.claim: The kill switch is read on launch and every 10 minutes, so running clients can keep syncing for up to 10 minutes after a disable. The artifact does not say how in-flight uploads or open conflict prompts are handled when sync stops.
attacks.evidence: 'Kill switch `cross_save_enabled=false` (server config, read on launch and every 10 min)'

attacks.claim: Alerts cover sync error rate, API 5xx and restore spikes, but not rejected or unloadable blobs, checksum failures, or the automatic kill-switch flip. Silent subset data issues could stay under threshold.
attacks.evidence: 'Alerts: sync error rate > 2% for 15 min, API 5xx > 1%, any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate.'

attacks.claim: The $600 hard stop depends on billing data that can lag, and no trigger latency is given. The $250 alert has no stated action, and no per-launch request budget bounds sync or conflict loops.
attacks.evidence: 'hard project budget stop at $600/month; at the stop, the kill switch below is flipped automatically.' and 'Requests and egress ~$90/month.'

attacks.claim: The storage forecast (~140 GB, ~$3/month) omits the slots-per-player and version-count assumptions, so it cannot be reproduced. The averages are coherent, so this is a missing assumption rather than a calculation error.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage: ~420 KB per slot × up to 5 versions; forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month.'

attacks.claim: The 30k-launch load test covers under a third of the ~109k opt-in players and gives no peak-concurrency derivation. Opt-in spreads load, but the patch reaches all players at once, so the launch-day peak is not modelled.
attacks.evidence: 'Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min | p95 410 ms, 0 errors' and 'Dec 2 10:00 PT: 1.4 to all players on both stores'

attacks.claim: There is no staged enablement for sync. The kill switch is global, and Cross-Save is available to everyone who opts in on day one, so a sync defect cannot be limited to a cohort first.
attacks.evidence: 'Cross-Save available to everyone who turns it on.' and 'Kill switch cross_save_enabled=false' with no cohort control

attacks.claim: A closed, banned or lost store account can permanently block the remaining account, because linking and unlinking both need valid sessions from both stores. Concurrent link requests from two PCs may also pass the 'already linked' check, since no transactional constraint is described.
attacks.evidence: 'Each store account can be in at most one link.' and 'Linking requires valid sessions from both stores at the same time.' ABSENT: transactional uniqueness and one-sided unlink path.

attacks.claim: The checksum is a client-side integrity check, not an authenticity guarantee. A modified client can upload a blob that other devices download as newest, and no signing or server-side integrity rule is described.
attacks.evidence: 'The client verifies the save's checksum and v3 schema before loading' ABSENT: signing or server-side integrity over blobs.

attacks.claim: Screen-narration QA covers only the conflict prompt. The sync status line, the 'local save was kept' failure message and the Restore list, which communicate data-safety state, are not in the accessibility checks.
attacks.evidence: 'screen narration for the conflict prompt | Pass'

attacks.claim: Relative timestamps such as 'today 18:02' are ambiguous across time zones and device clock errors, and this is exactly when the conflict choice matters most.
attacks.evidence: 'Keep the save on this PC (12 h 41 m, today 18:02) or the cloud save (13 h 05 m, today 21:40)?'

attacks.claim: Linking depends on two third-party identity systems and all data sits in one Frankfurt region. A store API or policy change could break linking, and no exit or migration path for existing links is documented.
attacks.evidence: 'Storage region: EU (Frankfurt) for all players.' and 'Steam OpenID / Epic Account Services'

attacks.claim: The sidecar design depends on 1.3 ignoring unknown files, and no CI test pins that behaviour, so a future 1.3 build or store-folder cleanup could break it silently.
attacks.evidence: '1.3 ignores the sidecar' ABSENT: CI test pinning 1.3 behaviour.

attacks.claim: The counsel review of PP-v6 has no date or scope, and the Epic listing change is not shown as ordered before the 2026-12-02 launch.
attacks.evidence: 'reviewed by our counsel (PP-v6)' and 'Epic store page "online features" updated to list optional account linking'

attacks.claim: Two gameplay modifiers and 31 bug fixes ship with a data-touching feature, so a modifier or fix defect cannot be reverted without also reverting cross-save, and reverting to 1.3 also removes the fixes.
attacks.evidence: 'Two new difficulty modifiers and 31 bug fixes' and '1.3 is restored as the default branch on both stores'
